mechanism_claims.claim_text: Chemerin-derived peptide 4 (Val66-Pro85) is the primary antimicrobial region recovered in this paper, supported by overlapping peptide screening and Table 3 MIC results.
mechanism_claims.limitations: This is domain/activity mapping, not a molecular target claim.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: p4 causes direct bacterial lysis in an E. coli JM83 beta-galactosidase release assay at 10 µM, with pH and salt dependence shown in Figure 5.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: chemerin peptide 4 against E. coli JM83
mechanism_claims.limitations: The source supports direct lysis context but does not define the result as an LC50 value.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: p4 antimicrobial potency is discussed as charge-governed with possible hydrophobic contribution; this is source-stated mechanistic interpretation, not a quantified membrane biophysics assay.
mechanism_claims.limitations: No receptor, enzyme target, or mammalian cytotoxicity mechanism is promoted.

evidence_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism adjudication from Figures 3-5, Table 2, Table 3, and linked database rows; generic framework locator notes were replaced.

caution_findings.evidence_context: Figure 5 supports lysis at 10 µM, but database LC/LC50 labels are not promoted to primary-source LC/LC50 activity records.
No local source hemolysis/cytotoxicity mechanism assay was recovered.
